layers.note: A herb of wet subalpine meadows, seeps and snowmelt flats, often in dense patches.

moisture.note: Wet ground: seeps, stream margins and saturated meadow by melting snow.

heat_load.note: Any aspect; where snow lies late.

elevation_m.note: Montane to alpine; lower in the north.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −20 to 1 °C; gone below −30 °C and above 5 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −42 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −50 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 6 to 17 °C; gone below 4 °C, where summers are too short, and above 20 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 600 to 3,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 300.

degree_days_5.note: About 150 to 1,600 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 50.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.5, gone by 0.35.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). White marsh marigold grows from Alaska to Arizona and New Mexico in wet mountain meadows (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
